text:
alice: Quick sync — I'm trying to make a short, repeatable checklist for our bench probe runs so apples-to-apples comparisons are reliable. Posting proposed steps, defs for TTFT/TPOT, and probes for KV priming. Please skim and flag anything missing.

ben: thanks — can you state precisely how we're defining TTFT vs TPOT here? we keep mixing semantics in tickets.

carla: my proposal: TTFT = time from request accepted by runtime (after auth/rate-limit) to first generated token leaving the runtime (first byte). TPOT = time from request accepted to final token emitted + any client-side post-processing (so includes streaming tail). keep both measured at server side where possible.

dave: ok makes sense. do we exclude network serialization and client RTT? we want kernel/runtime-only numbers for kernel-selection comparisons.

carla: yes — instrument at the rpc boundary inside the runtime. record both server-side and end-to-end for customer-facing metrics, but canonical bench numbers are server-side.

alice: exact checklist I'm proposing: 1) pin model and kernel binary (document kernel selection) 2) disable autoscaling/burst 3) run 3 warmup passes with KV priming disabled, then 3 with KV priming enabled (to capture cold vs hot) 4) run replay harness with identical time-of-day traffic mapping for 60s steady-state windows 5) collect TTFT/TPOT/p50/p95/p99/goodput/QPS and raw perf traces 6) attach kernel selection mapping and batch-size histograms for each run 7) keep cache hit telemetry and missed-prefix traces for regression triage.

ben: small nit — for step 3, please define "KV priming" command so infra team can automate.

alice: sure — example:```bash
# prime kv for user-session prefixes
python tools/replay_tool.py --mode=prime --duration=30 --prefix-db priming_set.json --target=runtime:12345
# steady-state test
python tools/replay_tool.py --mode=replay --profile=staging_profile.json --duration=60 --emit-metrics
```

dave: what about batching heuristics? do we enforce a fixed batch cap and a fixed batching window for the run?

carla: we need two lanes: 1) controlled bench where batch cap + batch latency window are fixed (for apples-to-apples kernel comparisons), 2) adaptive lane that mirrors production policy for cost/quality tradeoffs. report both.

alice: agreed. add to checklist: capture batch size distribution + wait-time histograms. also snapshot kernel decision logs (which kernel chosen per request/step).

ben: how do we compute goodput vs QPS here? I've seen goodput used differently across teams.

carla: goodput = number of successfully completed inference tokens (or requests that meet SLO) per second of runtime work — basically the useful output rate after filtering retries/fallbacks. QPS = raw request acceptance rate at the gateway. We report both and a conversion factor = goodput/QPS.

dave: prefer including dropped/failed request counts and fallback-model invocations as separate columns in the run CSV. makes regression triage easier.

alice: agreed. I'll add columns: request_id, kernel_id, batch_size, kv_cache_hit (bool), ttft_ms, tpot_ms, goodput_tokens, qps_snapshot, fallback_reason, error_code.

perf-bot: automated summary attached — kernel=fast-attn-v2 selected 74% of steps, avg batch=6.2, kv_hit=0.81, ttft_p95=42ms, tpot_p95=120ms. CI diff: ttft_p95 +12ms vs baseline.

carla: thanks perf-bot. that +12ms is suspicious; can someone link the kernel change? was there a quant path swap?

alice: looks like kernel selector was updated in the last deploy to prefer quantized kernels for >512 seq len. I'll trigger a targeted run with the old selector to reproduce.

ben: can we add a tiny profiling snippet to export kernel-level timelines? e.g., tracepoints per kernel call and batch merge time.

alice: yes — extract trace with `./bin/trace_export --range start..end --format json` and attach with runs. put trace id in run metadata.

dave: final ask from me — add a small reproducibility tag to each run: git_sha, kernel_bin_sha, env_vars snapshot. otherwise we keep chasing ghosts.

alice: will update the doc and push to the runbook. thanks all — if nobody objects I'll start automating these steps into bench-ci tomorrow :thumbsup:

carla: :thumbsup: looks good.

ben: thanks, lgtm.

perf-bot: note: if CI run shows >10% regression in p95 TTFT, auto-open perf-incident in incidents channel.
